reply.text: Disabled on sent lines, with the reason under it.

title: Ring first
text: When nothing is selected and a barista taps a drink, should that start a new order, with the tab or name attached afterwards and no guest count asked?
why: Decides where every order starts. Most tills start with the item; the till already rings first, and this makes it a ruling.

options.label: Ring first
options.desc: tap a drink, attach a tab after
options.then: the counter and the table start the same way

options.label: Tab first
options.desc: pick or open a tab, then ring
options.then: every walk-up needs a tab before the first tap

title: The usual choice on close
text: When a drink has a usual choice (the house milk) and the barista closes the options sheet without pressing Add, should the drink go on with the usual choice?
why: One tap for the usual drink, or a cancel like most tills. Choices with no usual still block either way.

options.label: Closing adds it with the usual choice

title: Paying by card with the wifi down
text: With the wifi down, how does a guest who wants to pay by card leave paid?
why: Today the bill never opens offline, so the walk is stuck: a guest paying by card cannot leave paid. Each answer is a different build.

options.label: The card terminal takes it offline
options.then: the terminal stores the payment and sends it when it is back; a small risk of a later decline

options.label: A payment link on the guest's phone
options.then: the guest pays on their own data; the till shows a code to scan

options.label: Keep the tab open
options.then: the guest pays next visit; only for guests the shop knows
